spans.text: A mod can add rows to the Phigros++ tab of the game's settings. Phigros++ saves what the player picks, so it's the same after a restart.

blocks.text:
local enabled = setting("Say hello", true)                 -- a toggle, on by default
local times = setting("Times", 3, { 1, 10 })               -- a slider from 1 to 10
local mood = setting("Mood", "happy", { "happy", "sleepy" }) -- a choice, a tap picks the next one

button("Say it now", function()
  for _ = 1, times() do toast("Hello, I'm " .. mood()) end
end)

if enabled() then toast("Hello!") end

spans.text: gives back a function: call it to read the current value. Calling it with a value changes the setting, as if the player had.
The label is also the name the value is saved under, so it can be used only once across all mods: a second
with the same label stops the mod from loading. Pick labels that say what they do, like "Say hello" rather than "Enabled".

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.summary: playing a chart with other players at the same time, and the socket that carries it

spans.text: A room is a group of up to 8 players who play the same chart at the same time and see each other's scores, and up to 8 spectators who watch them play. Rooms live on phigros.tools, so a player needs a profile there (
talks to the server and follows the match,
draws the rooms and the room.
The tab with two people next to the chapter screen's leaderboard lists the open rooms (
), with "Create a room" on its right. Its top bar reads Rooms and Friends: tapping Friends shows the player's friends instead (

). A room has a name (24 characters at most, links are taken out, the player's name when empty) and may have a password: only the players who type it join, and nothing of what such a room plays shows on phigros.tools. A room without one is open to anyone, shows live on
and keeps its matches there. That page's "Join in Phigros++" is a
link: it opens the game in the room, asking for the password when there's one. Invite, in the room, lists the player's friends who are online (
): a tap sends one a toast that joins the room.

The room's screen covers the menus. Its players are on the left, in the order they joined: the first is the host, under a golden crown, and the next one takes over when the host leaves. The chart to play is on the right with its difficulty and modifiers, the chat under the players. Chat lines only go to the players in the room: the server passes them on without keeping them, and the site never gets them.

Anyone adds charts to the room. Add chart hides the screen so the player can browse the game: playing a chart from the song list adds it to the room instead of starting it, at the level and with the modifiers picked there (

). The room is on the first chart added and queues the others after it, 20 at most and 3 from one player: they show under the chart as Up next, each with its level and who added it. The player who added a chart, or the host, takes it back with its cross, and the host orders the queue: holding a chart, then dragging it to its place. Rooms play the game's own EZ, HD, IN and AT charts, not custom ones.

Everyone plays the room's chart their own way. A player's row shows the level and modifiers they play it with: as the chart was added, until they tap the level under the cover (which goes to the next level of the song they have unlocked) or Modifiers. A chart with effects of its own plays without modifiers, as it does alone. A match ranks its plays by the total their modifiers give the score, whatever the levels played.
Tapping a player's row, anyone can ask them to be a friend, and the host can make them host instead or remove them, who then can't join that room again. Tapping the room's name renames it.

Each game tells the room whether it has the chart unlocked at the level its player picked. A player who doesn't is marked "No chart" and sits the match out, unless they pick a level they have: a room never gives a song the player doesn't own. The others tap Ready, and once everyone who has the chart is ready the host's Start sends them all into it, through the song list's own start (
). A chart played with Random is shuffled from a seed the server draws, the same for everyone.

A play in a room is a play like any other: recorded, saved by the game when it has no modifiers, and sent to phigros.tools with the player's toggles. While it lasts, the room's scores show on the left of the screen, best first ("Show the room's scores while playing").
